headline: Council adopts Kahoʻolawe resolution, discusses Bills 74 and 75, refers Bill 68

meeting.summary: Bill 74 would let emergency funds pay county costs and aid for all recent severe weather events. Bill 75 would grant $6 million to Hawaiʻi Community Lending for the Lahaina Residential rebuild. Bill 68 went to the Water and Infrastructure Committee with no objections.
meeting.recap: The lawyer said that if the award is not funded, firefighters get no raises.[[1:57:18]] Bill 74 would let emergency funds pay county costs and aid for all recent severe weather events.[[2:27:03]] Bill 75 would grant $6 million to Hawaiʻi Community Lending for the Lahaina Residential rebuild.[[2:31:03]] A council member said homes with 12 or 17 bedrooms are spreading on narrow Lahaina streets.[[3:02:25]] Bill 30 adds $3.5 million for the Central Maui Regional Wastewater Reclamation Facility in Waikapū.[[3:07:20]]
decided: With no objections, the special parking bill was sent to the Water and Infrastructure Committee.
meeting.next: The chair said she already sent a letter asking for an itemized breakdown of emergency fund spending.

moments.q: "This is actually a disappointing slap in the face."
"If it's not funded, they don't get anything."

issues.oneLine: Bill 47 changes off-street parking requirements for housing.

deadlines.t: End of planned County help with costs of continued housing under the state's interim housing program.

issues.brief: The deputy housing director said ADUs (accessory dwelling units, small extra homes on a lot) with two or more bedrooms would need two or more parking stalls.[[#1]] The department said 40% of the ADUs funded by its ʻohana assistance program have two bedrooms.[[#2]]
